examples.text: Herr Weckherlin hatte einen dummen Witz gemacht, und Labude war daran gestorben. Es war nur scheinbar ein Selbstmord gewesen. […] Er [Weckherlin] hatte ihm vergiftete Worte ins Ohr geträufelt, wie Arsenik ins Trinkglas.

glosses: A very thin river.

examples.text: The brook had shrunk to a mere trickle.

glosses: A very thin flow; the sound of such a flow.

examples.text: The tap of the washbasin in my bedroom is leaking and the trickle drives me mad at night.
The streams that run south and east from the mountains to the coast are short and rapid torrents after a storm, but at other times dwindle to feeble trickles of mud.

glosses: to pour a liquid in a very thin stream, or so that drops fall continuously.

examples.text: The doctor trickled some iodine on the wound.

glosses: to flow in a very thin stream or drop continuously.

examples.text: Here the water just trickles along, but later it becomes a torrent.
The film was so bad that people trickled out of the cinema before its end.
Her white night-dress was smeared with blood, and a thin stream trickled down the man's bare chest which was shown by his torn-open dress.

The period of intensive traffic is over by about 5.30 p.m. and for the rest of the evening steadily diminishes, the main activity being the Channel Islands boat trains which trickle in after about 6.30 p.m. and depart again for Weymouth an hour or so later.

glosses: To move or roll slowly.

examples.text: Some [marbles] were found in a child's grave at Nagada, Egypt […] together with a set of ninepins and three rectangular bricks which could have formed an arch through which to trickle the balls.
Their only shot of the first period was a long-range strike from top-scorer Ebanks-Blake which trickled tamely wide.

glosses: To fall one drop at a time.

examples.text: Listening to the tap next door drip all night drove me mad!

glosses: To leak slowly.

examples.text: Does the sink drip, or have I just spilt water over the floor?

glosses: To let fall in drops.

examples.text: After putting oil on the side of the salad, the chef should drip a little vinegar in the oil.
My broken pen dripped ink onto the table.

c. 1726, Alexander Pope (probable author), The Lamentation of Glumdalclitch
Which from the thatch drips fast a shower of rain.

Philander went into the next room[…]and came back with a salt mackerel that dripped brine like a rainstorm. Then he put the coffee pot on the stove and rummaged out a loaf of dry bread and some hardtack.

glosses: To have a superabundance of (something).

examples.text: The Old Hall simply drips with masterpieces of the Flemish painters.
The duchess was dripping with jewels.

glosses: To rain lightly; to drizzle.

examples.text: The weather isn't so bad. I mean, it's dripping, but you're not going to get so wet.

glosses: To be wet, to be soaked.
To whine or complain consistently; to grumble.

examples.text: The Women's Royal Naval Service was integrated with the Royal Navy in November 1993. […] Men interviewed by Public Eye (April, 1994) said they should 'stop dripping about it' and that women should learn to 'take it like a man […]

glosses: Be impressive or attractive.

examples.text: I'm sorry for drippin', but drip is what I do. And one of these days, I'm gon' get dressed and drip all over you.

glosses: A drop of a liquid.

examples.text: I put a drip of vanilla extract in my hot cocoa.
I need a bucket to catch the drips.

glosses: A falling or letting fall in drops; act of dripping.

examples.text: the light drip of the suspended oar

glosses: An apparatus that slowly releases a liquid, especially one that intravenously releases drugs into a patient's bloodstream.

examples.text: He's not doing so well. The doctors have put him on a drip.

glosses: A limp, ineffectual, or uninteresting person.

examples.text: He couldn't even summon up the courage to ask her name... what a drip!

Because most of the blokes I fancy think l'm stupid and pointless—and, so, they just bonk me and then leave me. And the kind of blokes that do fancy me, I think are drips. I can't even be bothered to bonk them. Which does sort of leave me a bit nowhere.

glosses: That part of a cornice, sill course, or other horizontal member, which projects beyond the rest, and has a section designed to throw off rainwater.

examples.text: His drip is looking fine, especially the Supreme t-shirt.
